title: Norwegian Stockfish sea cooked dried cod four stock fish head - 5lbs
description: The word “Stockfish” represents any of the species of certain salt-water fish (Cod, Tusk, Haddock, Sey, or Ling) that has been completely de-hydrated, with no added salt or preservatives. The cleaned fresh fish with head and entrails removed are tied in pairs at the tail and hung on wooden racks to dry in natural fresh cold air (January – April). The drying process takes approximately three to four months, during which 70% of the water is removed and the essential vitamins and nutrients are retained. The de-hydrated fish (STOCKFISH) acquires a peculiar flavor/taste that is totally different from the fresh fish flavor. The nutritional value of 1-Kg of stockfish is the same as approx. 5-Kg of fresh fish. Stockfish is one of the richest known sources of protein, Calcium, Iron and B-Vitamins. Stockfish can be adapted to suite most tastes and palates. When adequately soaked, the fish regains its original weight, and the flesh becomes milky. The fish can be cooked in the same way as fresh cod-fish – poached, fried, creamed or grilled – and can be used in a wide variety of nutritional and tasty dishes.

title: Norwegian Hard Stockfish Stake – Premium Round Cod Fish: 1-lbs Cut
description: The word “Stockfish” represents any of the species of certain salt-water fish (Cod, Tusk, Haddock, Sey, or Ling) that has been completely de-hydrated, with no added salt or preservatives. The cleaned fresh fish with head and entrails removed are tied in pairs at the tail and hung on wooden racks to dry in natural fresh cold air (January – April). The drying process takes approximately three to four months, during which 70% of the water is removed and the essential vitamins and nutrients are retained. The de-hydrated fish (STOCKFISH) acquires a peculiar flavor/taste that is totally different from the fresh fish flavor. The nutritional value of 1-Kg of stockfish is the same as approx. 5-Kg of fresh fish. Stockfish is one of the richest known sources of protein, Calcium, Iron and B-Vitamins. Stockfish can be adapted to suite most tastes and palates. When adequately soaked, the fish regains its original weight, and the flesh becomes milky. The fish can be cooked in the same way as fresh cod-fish – poached, fried, creamed or grilled – and can be used in a wide variety of nutritional and tasty dishes. When stored in a dry, non-humid and cool place, stockfish can keep indefinitely.

title: Norwegian Hard Stockfish Stake – Premium Round Dried Cod Fish: 2-lbs Cut
description: The word “Stockfish” represents any of the species of certain salt-water fish (Cod, Tusk, Haddock, Sey, or Ling) that has been completely de-hydrated, with no added salt or preservatives. The cleaned fresh fish with head and entrails removed are tied in pairs at the tail and hung on wooden racks to dry in natural fresh cold air (January – April). The drying process takes approximately three to four months, during which 70% of the water is removed and the essential vitamins and nutrients are retained. The de-hydrated fish (STOCKFISH) acquires a peculiar flavor/taste that is totally different from the fresh fish flavor. The nutritional value of 1-Kg of stockfish is the same as approx. 5-Kg of fresh fish. Stockfish is one of the richest known sources of protein, Calcium, Iron and B-Vitamins. Stockfish can be adapted to suite most tastes and palates. When adequately soaked, the fish regains its original weight, and the flesh becomes milky. The fish can be cooked in the same way as fresh cod-fish – poached, fried, creamed or grilled – and can be used in a wide variety of nutritional and tasty dishes. When stored in a dry, non-humid and cool place, stockfish can keep indefinitely.

Your wild salmon fillets have been quick-frozen to lock in their flavor and nutrients, and shipped to you on dry ice. Upon arrival, please freeze or refrigerate. Fillets will keep in the freezer for approximately 3-4 months; once thawed they should be cooked and used within 1-2 days. Once a frozen fillet is completely thawed, it can be re-frozen though we do not recommend it, as taste and quality may begin to suffer. No fillet should be re-frozen if it has been thawed 2 days or longer.

Regardless of how you like to cook your salmon (bake, broil, grill, sauté or poach), we believe the key to success is to SLOW DOWN! Slow cooking locks in the natural juices of the salmon, for a more succulent flavor. When the salmon has turned from translucent to just about completely opaque the salmon is done. At this point the salmon should begin to flake easily with a fork. It is important to note that once removed from the heat, your salmon will continue to cook for several more minutes. Here are some specific guidelines by cooking method:

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven’s middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

title: Wild Alaska SOCKEYE Salmon - 10lb Box of Boneless 6oz Portioned Fillets
bullet_point: [10LB WILD SOCKEYE SALMON BONELESS 6OZ PORTIONS]
description:
Packaging:
Our orders are carefully packed using dry ice inside insulated inserts in a corrugated shipping box. Your fish will remain frozen for you to put right in the freezer until you’re ready to eat!

Thawing:
It’s best to thaw seafood overnight in the refrigerator. Place the package on a plate or shallow pan to catch any liquid and allow 8-10 hours (for full fillets).

Never allow seafood to thaw at room temperature or place in water to thaw. Flavor and texture are both lost this way.

About Our Product:
Our sockeye salmon is wild caught and has a flavor that is unrivaled because our process is simple. We catch and process only our fish. All of our fish is processed and flash frozen within hours of harvest. This keeps the fish fresh and helps maintain the nutrients and flavor that so many of our customers are searching for. Each individually seal portion is aproximately 6 ounces and can contain between 1,500-2,000mg of Omega-3’s and close to 1,110 IU of Vitamin D3. 10 lbs. of sockeye can vary form 16 to 20 individual steak packets.

Wild Alaskan Sockeye Salmon are a sustainably managed species by the state of Alaska, and many health organizations, included but not limited to, the EPA and FDA, view Sockeye Salmon as one of the cleanest of all ocean fish. As a 100% fisherman family owned small business, we believe in one thing: providing you with a product that we are equally as excited to eat. The quality and taste are unsurpassed and the level of freshness can only get better if you join us on the boat! Portion fillets range in size from 6-12 oz. each depending on the size of the fish they are hand cut from. Each piece serves 1-2 people. The 10 lb. box contains roughly 20 - 30 pieces. Our portioned fillets make for an easy dinner option any day of the week.

Preparation

description: Trancio di Tonno Rosso is a simple fillet, the leanest part of the fish - but this is a far cry from ordinary canned tuna, with its dry, chalky texture and bland taste. The exquisite Mediterranean Bluefin Tuna, or Tonno Rosso is full of fresh flavor and and can be enjoyed right out of the can with a squeeze of lemon and a few drops of balsamic. Mix it with cooked beans, asparagus, boiled potatoes, roasted red tomatoes, and sweet onions for a delicious and healthy Mediterranean feast. Based in Erice, Conservificio Tre Torri continues to prepare tuna with artisanal methods generations old. These Mediterranean Bluefin Tuna are never frozen and he entire production is done by hand; when the tuna arrives. It is butchered, and the cuts are selected and separated for ventresca, tarantello, and trancio. It is boiled in small batches, cooled, and canned using local Sicilian olive oil and sea salt from Trapani. Uncontrolled fishing has wreaked havoc on the tuna population, and Gustiamo is proud to support a small producer who continues to use tuna fished sustainably, with the traditional net and hook methods. Tre Torri produces a very small quantity of canned tuna - about 88,000 pounds a year - which is the amount some industrial plants process in one day. Producing this way is very expensive, and the price of Tre Torri una reflects the real cost of this Mediterranean delicacy. This is a Bluefin Tuna you can truly feel good about enjoying.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

description: Ventresca, the belly of the tuna, is prized by seafood connoisseurs as the most tender and delicious part of the entire tuna. Ventresca is widely known as the finest part of the Bonito del Norte tuna and Nardin makes the finest tuna in Spain. Nardin Ventresca Belly Fillets are line caught, hand prepared and packed in olive oil - resulting in the most tender, flavorful tuna you'll ever eat! The Bonito del Norte tuna is a small type of Albacore tuna that migrates annually from the Atlantic Ocean to the cool seas of Northern Spain. Once off the coast of Spain, the tuna lingers and fattens up on the plentiful smaller fish there. Only then are they are ready for harvest. The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. About the company: Scalia Benedetto has been one of the top Sicilian companies for preserving fish since 1973. They are not as large or as old as their major competitors, but this allows them to do things the old fashion way and the difference shows up in the flavor and texture of their oil packed and salt packed anchovies. The company was founded by Benedetto Scalia in Sciacca Thermae, on the Agrigento coast of Southwest Sicily, a city famous for its an important fishing fleet. Their anchovy products are carefully processed by the women of Sciacca using traditional handicraft techniques. What is most important about these little Sicilian blue fish is that they are only taken during the proper season - otherwise they will have a "mushy" texture when they are preserved - and cleaned and salted as soon as possible after they are caught. Because of Scalia's attention to detail it is possible to discover the flavor and texture of the ancient Mediterranean. The Italians, from one end of the peninsula to the other use these little, aromatic, preserved fish in almost any conceivable recipe. While those in the south seem to use them with the same frequency they use olive oil, they also show up in numerous sauces, salads, and other dishes in the northern Italy.

description: In Alaska the fishery is typically January through March with a secondary fishery September through October. Cod is one of the most universally used and versatile fish species, as it is caught in so many parts of the world's oceans and used by so many world markets in a variety of product forms. While atlantic and pacific cod are two distinct species, there is very little, if any, difference between the two as product forms. Atlantic cod occupies some eastern United States and European market niches as it has been fished commercially for much longer. As atlantic cod stocks dwindle, however, pacific cod products have made their way into these niches. Pacific cod is also known as true cod, Alaskan cod and "P"-cod. Black cod, ling cod and rock cod are not related to "true" cods.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

The method involves attracting a school of tuna to the side of a baitboat by throwing live sardines and anchovies overboard. This creates a tuna feeding frenzy and fish are hauled out of the water, one-by-one, using pole and line with an artificial lure attached. description:
Your wild salmon fillets have been quick-frozen to lock in their flavor and nutrients, and shipped to you on dry ice. Upon arrival, please freeze or refrigerate. Fillets will keep in the freezer for approximately 3-4 months; once thawed they should be cooked and used within 1-2 days. Once a frozen fillet is completely thawed, it can be re-frozen though we do not recommend it, as taste and quality may begin to suffer. No fillet should be re-frozen if it has been thawed 2 days or longer.

The best way to thaw your wild salmon fillet is to leave it in the refrigerator overnight (in its pouch), allowing at least 8-10 hours. Trying to rush the process by thawing at room temperature or placing the frozen pouch in warm water is definitely NOT recommended, as it can cause the salmon to lose flavor and texture. If you must thaw your salmon quickly, place the frozen pouch in a bowl of cool water for 30-45 minutes, and then continue thawing in refrigerator.

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven's middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

description:
Three hundred miles of unrelenting river requires Copper Salmon to store a remarkable amount of nutrients so they can muscle their way up the 300-hundred mile long and treacherous rapids.This makes Copper River Sockeye simply the best salmon in the world.

Copper River Seafoods was started in 1996 by four dedicated Alaskan fishermen with two things in common; a passion for Alaska wild salmon and a belief in sustainable fishing.

Wild Copper River Sockeye Salmon are world-renowned for their full flavor and distinctively deep red color. They're naturally packed with omega-3 EPA and DHA fatty acids (1,570 mg per 2 oz serving), a nutrient which has been linked to cardio vascular health, muscle development, reducing inflammation,eye care, and may even boost your metabolism.

The Copper River Sockeye Salmon arrive at our smoke house in Cordova, Alaska within 24 hours from the time they are caught. The fish are filleted by hand to ensure the highest quality possible, then put into our traditional curing brine, which gives it the delicious taste that our smoked salmon is famous for. The cured salmon is then smoked to perfection with natural Alder wood. Finally, the salmon is hand packed into a gold foil pouch and cooked in its natural Omega-3 oils. Simply place onto crackers with cream cheese and serve!

Make a delicious smoked salmon dip: mix smoked salmon, mayo (or cream cheese), diced onions, pickles, and green pepper into a food processor and pulse until smooth. If you want a little heat add one small Jalapeno pepper --or a dash of Red Pepper flakes. Add salt & pepper and serve.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

description: This dried anchovy also known as Hardenberg's anchovy is a small schooling fish found in depth of 20-50m in most of the tropical areas of the Indo-pacific oceans including Madagascar and Mauritius eastward and towards Australia and further east to Samoa in westwards. Maximum length do not exceed 15.5 cm. It has 15 to 17 dorsal soft rays and 18 to 21 anal soft rays. There are 2 to 6 small needle-like scutes on the belly region. Maxilla tip is pointed, reaching front border of pre-operculum. Body is a typical engraulid form with light transparent fleshy brown, and silver stripe down flank. Indian anchovy usually feeds on planktons. This fish is part of the cuisine of the South- and Southeast Asian marine regions. It can be crisp-fried, used to make fish-based culinary products like fish sauce or in curries. In Sri Lanka, this variety of fish is made into a tasty snack by dipping in a batter of flour, then rolled in bread crumbs and deep fried in oil. It is also popular as a ‘white curry’, i.e.a curry made with coconut milk. A spicier variant is made with dry chilli gravy and served with scraped fresh coconut to offset the hotness of the gravy.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved. We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

description:
The Royal Fillet is the richest part of the salmon. The fillet is boneless, succulent and flavorful to the bite. The whole fillet is lightly smoked and meant to be served uncooked and cut into sashimi-like slices.

Our Story

When Harry (Aaron) Forman arrived in London’s East End from Russia at the beginning of the last century he pursued the trade he knew best – curing fish; in particular, the salmon he imported in barrels of brine from the Baltic. It wasn’t long, however, before he discovered a rich source of fresh wild salmon much closer to home: Scotland.

Inspired by the exceptional quality of fresh Scottish salmon, Harry developed a cure that complemented its unrivalled flavour. The deliciously mild London Cure was born and soon it was the talk of reputable establishments around the capital such as Wilton's restaurant which we have supplied for over 90 years with our genuine wild smoked Scottish salmon.

A century later H. Forman & Son remains a family concern, the last of the original London smokeries, with Lance Forman, Harry’s great grandson, flying the flag for the famous London Cure. Remaining faithful to principles established in 1905 – the freshest salmon, a little salt, just the right amount of oak smoke – he is upholding traditional values and skills that would otherwise have died out long ago, along with one of gastronomy’s finest foods: H. Forman & Son’s Genuine Wild Smoked Scottish Salmon.

description:
Your wild salmon fillets have been quick-frozen to lock in their flavor and nutrients, and shipped to you on dry ice. Upon arrival, please freeze or refrigerate. Fillets will keep in the freezer for approximately 3-4 months; once thawed they should be cooked and used within 1-2 days.
Once a frozen fillet is completely thawed, it can be re-frozen though we do not recommend it, as taste and quality may begin to suffer. No fillet should be re-frozen if it has been thawed 2 days or longer.

The best way to thaw your wild salmon fillet is to leave it in the refrigerator overnight (in its pouch), allowing at least 8-10 hours. Trying to rush the process by thawing at room temperature or placing the frozen pouch in warm water is definitely NOT recommended, as it can cause the salmon to lose flavor and texture. If you must thaw your salmon quickly, place the frozen pouch in a bowl of cool water for 30-45 minutes, and then continue thawing in refrigerator.

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven’s middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

description: Catfish is truly an American aquaculture success story. It takes 18 to 24 months to grow catfish to market size (2 to 3 pounds). The meat of catfish is white to off white and has an iridescent translucency to it. Being a grain fed fish the meat has a consistently sweet, mild flavor. The moist dense meat has a firm texture and fewer flakes than the typical whitefish. With its mild flavor and unusual texture, catfish is as versatile as chicken. You can use bold sauces to mild seasonings and catfish will handle them all well. You can bake, broil, fry, grill or sauté catfish with great success.

description: A true symbol of Portuguese gastronomy, canned sardines are highly appreciated the World over and represent a market with great international potential. Cofaco was created in 1961, as the result of a merger of two large canneries in the Algarve – Centeno, Cumbrera & Ca. and Raul Folque & Filhos. Based in Vila Real de Santo António, they were, at the time, the largest Portuguese canning group. During the second half of the 20th century fishing started drying up along the Algarve coast, forcing fishermen to go further and further afield in search of the fish. To overcome this situation, the canning industry began to relocate, and in 1962 Cofaco settled in the Azores – an “oasis” in the Atlantic Ocean. Hence, a year later, a plant was officially inaugurated on the island of Pico, and production began at the first Cofaco factory in the Azores. It subsequently relocated to Ribeira Grande, where Cofaco inaugurated the industrial hub of Rabo de Peixe in 1994, and where it still concentrates a large part of its production. Currently, Cofaco is the largest industrial employer in the Azores archipelago, and has a significant bearing on the region’s GDP.

title: Norwegian Stockfish – Premium Round Cod Fish: 5-lbs Cut
description: The word “Stockfish” represents any of the species of certain salt-water fish (Cod, Tusk, Haddock, Sey, or Ling) that has been completely de-hydrated, with no added salt or preservatives. The cleaned fresh fish with head and entrails removed are tied in pairs at the tail and hung on wooden racks to dry in natural fresh cold air (January – April). The drying process takes approximately three to four months, during which 70% of the water is removed and the essential vitamins and nutrients are retained. The de-hydrated fish (STOCKFISH) acquires a peculiar flavor/taste that is totally different from the fresh fish flavor. The nutritional value of 1-Kg of stockfish is the same as approx. 5-Kg of fresh fish. Stockfish is one of the richest known sources of protein, Calcium, Iron and B-Vitamins. Stockfish can be adapted to suite most tastes and palates. When adequately soaked, the fish regains its original weight, and the flesh becomes milky. The fish can be cooked in the same way as fresh cod-fish – poached, fried, creamed or grilled – and can be used in a wide variety of nutritional and tasty dishes. When stored in a dry, non-humid and cool place, stockfish can keep indefinitely.

description: Karko / Kako Among these seasonings is 'karko'. 'Karko' is a salted large fish caught and produced exclusively in The Gambia in West Africa. Some of the towns that produce it in The Gambia are Banju, Comju and Ghana Town (a place near the beach in The Gambia where lots of Ghanaians reside). The delicacy has names such as 'sine', 'kosile', 'semine' but predominantly called 'karko', an onomatopoetic word that means hardness due to its stiff nature. The fish used for 'karko' is large and often cut into wanted sizes and salted with large quantity of salt for about 24 hours. Then it is dried up under the scorched sun for days to make the salt stick and dry alongside to preserve it - don't mistake “karko” for “mormorni” or “koobi” because the three are different from one another. This Item ships only from Ghana so you get it fresh from the Mankessim market

description: This large package of superior boquerones are enough to serve a whole tapas party! The delicate white anchovies are tender and delicious, a mild, flavorful tapa famous across Spain. They pair especially well with crusty bread and piquillo peppers or salads. Skewer them with a pickle and an olive and serve as tapas, or eat right out of the package for a satisfying snack. Our white anchovies have been chilled since they were plucked from the Atlantic Ocean, filleted by hand and packaged so that you can enjoy the freshest boquerones in America. Boquerones are a popular, tender white anchovy and a classic Spanish tapa. After their departure from the ocean, they are carefully hand cleaned in Spain and immediately pickled in vinegar, which “cooks” them. They are then packed in extra virgin olive oil, vinegar, sliced garlic and parsley. These delectable fillets are a classic dish in tapas bars across Spain. Delicately salted with a much milder taste than traditional anchovies, these boquerones marinate in olive oil, white wine vinegar, garlic and parsley and don’t taste very “fishy” at all. All boquerones in Spain are flash frozen for food safety reasons, before being thawed and prepared in extra virgin olive oil and vinegar. Anchovies and boquerones are exactly the same kind of fish, the only difference is that anchovies are heavily salted and boquerones are preserved with vinegar and olive oil.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven’s middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

description:
The simplicity of eel, salt and smoke allows for the incredible natural oils to enhance the culinary experience. Formans smoked Dutch eel loses none of the natural oils during the subtle smoking process.

Our Story

When Harry (Aaron) Forman arrived in London’s East End from Russia at the beginning of the last century he pursued the trade he knew best – curing fish; in particular, the salmon he imported in barrels of brine from the Baltic. It wasn’t long, however, before he discovered a rich source of fresh wild salmon much closer to home: Scotland.

Inspired by the exceptional quality of fresh Scottish salmon, Harry developed a cure that complemented its unrivalled flavour. The deliciously mild London Cure was born and soon it was the talk of reputable establishments around the capital such as Wilton's restaurant which we have supplied for over 90 years with our genuine wild smoked Scottish salmon.

A century later H. Forman & Son remains a family concern, the last of the original London smokeries, with Lance Forman, Harry’s great grandson, flying the flag for the famous London Cure. Remaining faithful to principles established in 1905 – the freshest salmon, a little salt, just the right amount of oak smoke – he is upholding traditional values and skills that would otherwise have died out long ago, along with one of gastronomy’s finest foods: H. Forman & Son’s Genuine Wild Smoked Scottish Salmon.

description: Atlantic salmon is farmed throughout the world, with Chile, British Columbia and Washington, Eastern Canada and Northern Europe the main farming regions. The fish are raised in large floating net pens. New technologies and improved animal husbandry have largely eliminated the need for antibiotics in the raising of Atlantic salmon. Farmed salmon have a carotenoid pigment (astaxanthin) added to the feed to give the flesh its orange-reddish color. Wild salmon receive these carotenoids by their diet which includes small crustaceans rich in these carotenoids. The meat is moderately firm and oily and will have a marbled look to it when raw. The flavor of Atlantic salmon is milder than the wild salmon species. Cooking methods that lend themselves well are baking, broiling, grilling, poaching and smoking.

description: Tarantello di Tonno Rosso is the abdominal muscle of the fish. These Mediterranean Bluefin Tuna are never frozen and he entire production is done by hand; when the tuna arrives. It is butchered, and the cuts are selected and separated for ventresca, tarantello, and trancio. It is boiled in small batches, cooled, and canned using local Sicilian olive oil and sea salt from Trapani. Uncontrolled fishing has wreaked havoc on the tuna population, and Gustiamo is proud to support a small producer who continues to use tuna fished sustainably, with the traditional net and hook methods. Tre Torri produces a very small quantity of canned tuna - about 88,000 pounds a year - which is the amount some industrial plants process in one day. description:
The London Cure smoked Scottish salmon is what H. Forman & Son is known for. Formans hand prepares every side of salmon, from the filleting to the rope hanging to the pin-bone removal to the hand carving. There's no sugar, no nitrites, no added coloring and no wet brine. You will receive the finest smoked Scottish salmon direct to your door.

Our Story

When Harry (Aaron) Forman arrived in London’s East End from Russia at the beginning of the last century he pursued the trade he knew best – curing fish; in particular, the salmon he imported in barrels of brine from the Baltic. It wasn’t long, however, before he discovered a rich source of fresh wild salmon much closer to home: Scotland.

Inspired by the exceptional quality of fresh Scottish salmon, Harry developed a cure that complemented its unrivalled flavour. The deliciously mild London Cure was born and soon it was the talk of reputable establishments around the capital such as Wilton's restaurant which we have supplied for over 90 years with our genuine wild smoked Scottish salmon.

A century later H. Forman & Son remains a family concern, the last of the original London smokeries, with Lance Forman, Harry’s great grandson, flying the flag for the famous London Cure. Remaining faithful to principles established in 1905 – the freshest salmon, a little salt, just the right amount of oak smoke – he is upholding traditional values and skills that would otherwise have died out long ago, along with one of gastronomy’s finest foods: H. Forman & Son’s Genuine Wild Smoked Scottish Salmon.

title: Karko Kako from Mankessim dry salted fish (100gram)
description: Karko / Kako Among these seasonings is 'karko'. 'Karko' is a salted large fish caught and produced exclusively in The Gambia in West Africa. Some of the towns that produce it in The Gambia are Banju, Comju and Ghana Town (a place near the beach in The Gambia where lots of Ghanaians reside). The delicacy has names such as 'sine', 'kosile', 'semine' but predominantly called 'karko', an onomatopoetic word that means hardness due to its stiff nature. The fish used for 'karko' is large and often cut into wanted sizes and salted with large quantity of salt for about 24 hours. Then it is dried up under the scorched sun for days to make the salt stick and dry alongside to preserve it - don't mistake “karko” for “mormorni” or “koobi” because the three are different from one another. This Item ships only from Ghana so you get it fresh from the Mankessim market

description:
Your wild salmon fillets have been quick-frozen to lock in their flavor and nutrients, and shipped to you on dry ice. Upon arrival, please freeze or refrigerate. Fillets will keep in the freezer for approximately 3-4 months; once thawed they should be cooked and used within 1-2 days.
Once a frozen fillet is completely thawed, it can be re-frozen though we do not recommend it, as taste and quality may begin to suffer. No fillet should be re-frozen if it has been thawed 2 days or longer.

The best way to thaw your wild salmon fillet is to leave it in the refrigerator overnight (in its pouch), allowing at least 8-10 hours. Trying to rush the process by thawing at room temperature or placing the frozen pouch in warm water is definitely NOT recommended, as it can cause the salmon to lose flavor and texture. If you must thaw your salmon quickly, place the frozen pouch in a bowl of cool water for 30-45 minutes, and then continue thawing in refrigerator.

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven’s middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

description: Anchovy fillets in virgin olive oil. Soft and tender with a subtle and well-balanced flavor. Gently cleaned by hand, and with just the right amount of saltiness. These premium quality anchovies are caught near Santoña, in the Bay of Biscay. The Santoña anchovy is famous for its quality and taste. Packed and cleaned by hand these anchovies are perfect as a tapa just as they are. You can always use them for salads, pastas, or sauces -- but the best way to enjoy them is by themselves. The producer: Don Bocarte is one of the most important gourmet seafood producers in Spain. Based on Santoña, they are pioneers in olive oil conservation of fish and seafood. The catch is sustainable and controlled. Only fished between April and June, when quality is at its best. The anchovies are processed as soon as they are caught. They are quickly salted to preserve all the flavor. Immediately after the anchovies are put in salt presses for a minimum of 8 months under controlled temperature and humidity to eliminate most of the fat and ensure proper maturation. Last part of the process washing and filleting, is all done by hand to ensure the best texture, appearance and of course flavor. All the care and attention to detail makes a big difference. Don Bocarte anchovies have been awarded in tasting national and internationally.

About Seattle Fish Company:
Seattle Fish Co is a multi-generational, family-owned business that has been supplying the highest-quality seafood for over 100 years. As the Rocky Mountain region’s largest supplier of fresh fish, we’re proud to provide an unparalleled selection of seafood coupled with a dedication to personal service. Seattle Fish Co. was founded in 1918 when Mose Iacino began transporting fresh seafood from Seattle, Washington to landlocked Denver, Colorado. Since its inception, Seattle Fish Co. has devoted itself to big-picture best practices—from sustainable, responsible sourcing to 24/7 handling and beyond. Although the Mile High City will always be our home, we travel the world to bring the oceans’ best straight to our customers.

description:
P-line was first developed to respond to a great challenge - to provide the best fishing line available. Introduced into the North American market in 1982, p-line immediately caught the attention of both freshwater and saltwater anglers. Its copolymer based technology delivered a thin diameter, soft, supple fishing line that brought many advantages into one line. It improved casting distances, gave a more natural presentation to lures and Baits and allowed for increased line capacity on reels. Today we continue to meet the high standards and expectations of the serious angler. Whether you are a tournament competitor or a weekend enthusiast you can depend on p-line to demonstrate superior strength, great cast ability and abrasion resistance that is unsurpassed on the water. Combining our experiences in copolymer and fluorocarbon technologies, p-line is on the leading edge of quality, high-performance fishing lines. We keep a pulse on what anglers are asking for, new applications, Baits, and techniques fishermen are encountering as they search for fish. P-line은 최고의 낚싯줄을 제공하는 큰 도전에 대응하기 위해 처음 개발되었습니다. 1982년 북미 시장에 도입된 p-line은 즉시 담수 낚시꾼과 바다 낚시꾼의 관심을 끌었습니다. 공중합체 기반 기술은 얇은 직경의 부드럽고 유연한 낚싯줄을 제공하여 한 줄에 많은 이점을 가져왔습니다. 캐스팅 거리를 개선하고, 루어와 미끼에 더 자연스러운 표현을 주었으며 릴의 라인 용량을 늘릴 수 있습니다. 오늘날 우리는 진지한 낚시꾼의 높은 기준과 기대치를 계속 충족하고 있습니다. 토너먼트 경쟁자이든 주말 애호가이든 p-line을 사용하여 우수한 강도, 훌륭한 주조 능력 및 물속에서 탁월한 내마모성을 보여줄 수 있습니다. 공중합체와 플루오로카본 기술에 대한 경험을 결합한 p-line은 고품질의 고성능 낚싯줄의 선두에 있습니다. 우리는 낚시꾼이 요구하는 것, 새로운 적용, 미끼 및 어부들이 물고기를 찾을 때 마주치는 기술에 대한 맥박을 유지합니다. p-line으로 낚시를 즐기고 소중한 자원을 보호하시길 바랍니다. 모든 사람들이 양질의 낚시 경험의 즐거움에 참여할 수 있도록 어업을 건강하게 유지하고 물을 깨끗하게 유지하기 위해 할 수 있는 일을 하십시오.

description:
FAQ's

What Do You Feed Your Salmon?

Our goal is to provide a long-term sustainable diet that meets all the nutritional requirements of King Salmon. The feed carries Certificates of Analysis from registered laboratories, is certified GMO-free and BSE-free, and all ingredients are fully traceable. The feed consists of fish meal (sourced from sustainable fisheries), fish oil, animal protein and oil, vegetable protein meals, wheat/starch, vitamins, and minerals including the antioxidant Astaxanthin.

Do You Dye Your Salmon?

No. Our salmon feed contains Astaxanthin which is naturally found in Algae and krill and is an essential micro-nutrient for salmon. It’s so important to the salmon that they have the capacity to store the Astaxanthin in their muscle tissue because that is what makes them pink. Astaxanthin is a powerful antioxidant that is also found in other foods including dietary supplements.

Is Your Environment Clean?

Throughout their life, our salmon experience arguably the cleanest rearing environment found anywhere in the world. As smolt, they are nurtured in the safe sanctuaries of our pure mountain fed streams before being transferred to sea farms located in the remote, crystal clear sea waters of the Marlborough Sounds.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

Sustainable Seas Albacore Tuna

Sustainable Seas sources tuna caught only by pole and line. There is virtually no by-catch associated with the trolling or pole and line techniques, which are regarded as the best fishing methods for tuna, a fact worth remembering when you buy.

Pole and line fishing has been practiced for centuries in several different parts of the world. The method involves attracting a school of tuna to the side of a baitboat by throwing live sardines and anchovies overboard. This creates a tuna feeding frenzy and fish are hauled out of the water, one-by-one, using pole and line with an artificial lure attached. The size of tuna caught this way is almost exclusively younger migratory tuna that are also lower in mercury than the older tuna caught deeper with long-lines. Rethink your relationship with the seas.BE SUSTAINABLE

description:
Your wild salmon fillets have been quick-frozen to lock in their flavor and nutrients, and shipped to you on dry ice. Upon arrival, please freeze or refrigerate. Fillets will keep in the freezer for approximately 3-4 months; once thawed they should be cooked and used within 1-2 days. Once a frozen fillet is completely thawed, it can be re-frozen though we do not recommend it, as taste and quality may begin to suffer. No fillet should be re-frozen if it has been thawed 2 days or longer.

Regardless of how you like to cook your salmon (bake, broil, grill, sauté or poach), we believe the key to success is to SLOW DOWN! Slow cooking locks in the natural juices of the salmon, for a more succulent flavor. When the salmon has turned from translucent to just about completely opaque the salmon is done. At this point the salmon should begin to flake easily with a fork. It is important to note that once removed from the heat, your salmon will continue to cook for several more minutes. Here are some specific guidelines by cooking method:

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven’s middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

description:
Long coveted by connoisseurs, anchovies packed in salt have a pure, intense flavor, undiluted by water or the flavors of oil. Once anchovies are harvested, they are packed in barrels and a layer of anchovies are packed in salt, which is then layered on with more anchovies. This stacking method builds pressure within the barrel and the salt preserves the small fish as it is absorbed into their flesh. These salt packed anchovies come to you direct from this curing process. No other liquids are added to draw off their distinctive flavor. To use these anchovies, simply soak them for 15-20 minutes in warm water, then lift out the spines and separate the two filets.

description: Atlantic salmon is farmed throughout the world, with Chile, British Columbia and Washington, Eastern Canada and Northern Europe the main farming regions. The fish are raised in large floating net pens. New technologies and improved animal husbandry have largely eliminated the need for antibiotics in the raising of Atlantic salmon. Farmed salmon have a carotenoid pigment (astaxanthin) added to the feed to give the flesh its orange-reddish color. Wild salmon receive these carotenoids by their diet which includes small crustaceans rich in these carotenoids. The meat is moderately firm and oily and will have a marbled look to it when raw. The flavor of Atlantic salmon is milder than the wild salmon species. Cooking methods that lend themselves well are baking, broiling, grilling, poaching and smoking.

description:
Pure, all natural albacore tuna fills this convenient, BPA-free 6 ounce pouch. Each pouch contains albacore tuna line caught from Pacific West Coast fisheries, packed in its own natural juices and cooked just once. A choice item for those seeking an all-natural albacore experience, the tuna is ready to eat right out of the pouch or as an addition to any family meal. Convenient and easy-to-open, these pouches last up to three years on a shelf and have a noticeably fresher taste than tuna out of a traditional can. At Oregon Seafood's' facility in Coos Bay, OR, the fish is hand processed at ice cold temperatures, placed in the pouch and cooked just once, free of any preservatives or fillers. The wild albacore found in these pouches have been line caught by American fishermen from Pacific West Coast sustainable fisheries. In fact, this albacore tuna is listed on Monterey Bay Aquarium's Seafood Watch's Super Green List as a Best of the Best choice item for their sustainability and excellent source of heart healthy omega-3 fatty acids.

El atún puro y natural de albacora llena esta práctica bolsa de 6 onzas sin BPA. Cada bolsa contiene una línea de atún albacore capturada de pesquerías de la Costa Oeste del Pacífico, empacada en sus propios jugos naturales y cocinada solo una vez. Un elemento de elección para aquellos que buscan una experiencia natural de albacora, el atún está listo para comer directamente de la bolsa o como adición a cualquier comida familiar. Prácticas y fáciles de abrir, estas bolsas duran hasta tres años en un estante y tienen un sabor notablemente más fresco que el atún de una lata tradicional. En las instalaciones de Oregon Seafood en Coos Bay, OR, el pescado se procesa a mano a temperaturas frías de hielo, se coloca en la bolsa y se cocina una sola vez, sin conservantes o rellenos. El albacore salvaje que se encuentra en estas bolsas ha sido la línea capturada por pescadores estadounidenses de pesquerías sostenibles de la costa oeste del Pacífico. De hecho, este atún albacore figura en la lista Super Green de Monterey Bay Aquarium's Seafood Watch como un artículo mejor de la mejor elección por su sostenibilidad y excelente fuente de ácidos grasos omega-3 saludables para el corazón.

Jeder Beutel enthält Alpakore-Thunfischschnur, die von der pazifikischen Westküstenangeln gefangen wird, verpackt in eigenen natürlichen Säften und nur einmal gekocht wird. Eine Wahl für diejenigen, die ein ganz natürliches Alpakore-Erlebnis suchen, der Thunfisch ist bereit, direkt aus dem Beutel zu essen oder als Ergänzung für jedes Familienessen zu verwenden. Praktisch und einfach zu öffnen, halten diese Beutel bis zu drei Jahre im Regal und haben einen spürbar frischeren Geschmack als Thunfisch aus einer traditionellen Dose. In Oregon Seafood Werkstätte in Coos Bay, OR, wird der Fisch bei eiskalten Temperaturen von Hand verarbeitet, in den Beutel gelegt und nur einmal gekocht, frei von jeglichen Konservierungsstoffen oder Füllstoffen. Das wilde Albacore in diesen Beuteln wurde von amerikanischen Anglern aus nachhaltiger Pacific West Coast gefangen. In der Tat ist dieser Albacore Thunfisch auf Monterey Bay Aquarium's Super Green List als beste Wahl für ihre Nachhaltigkeit und ausgezeichnete Herzquelle gesunder Omega-3-Fettsäuren.

Na verdade, este atum de albacore está listado na lista de produtos superverdes do relógio de frutos do mar Monterey Bay Aquarium, como o melhor dos melhores itens para sua sustentabilidade e excelente fonte de ácidos graxos ômega-3 saudáveis no coração.

description:
◆ What is FISHER QUEEN- DASHI PACK? ◆

For a more authentic dashi experience!

This pack contains 10 semi-permeable bags (similar to tea bags) of soup stock.

Unlike powdered stocks that dissolve in water, these bags contain nothing but raw seafood material.

Use in all sorts of cooking, from soups to noodle dishes to marinades.

◆ How to cook with Fisher Queen Dashi Pack ? ◆

1. Put one dashi-pack into 600ml of cold water for 5 minutes.

2. When water starts to boil, lower temperature to medium level.

3. Boil for another 5 minutes on medium temperature and take the dashi-pack out of the water.

◆ For The Best Result! ◆

Do not simmer together with other food.

Use ladle or wire skimmer to scoop out the dashi pack.

Do not squeeze pack after scooping out from pot.

Store in a cool, shaded place, away from direct sunlight.

description: The word “Stockfish” represents any of the species of certain salt-water fish (Cod, Tusk, Haddock, Sey, or Ling) that has been completely de-hydrated, with no added salt or preservatives. The cleaned fresh fish with head and entrails removed are tied in pairs at the tail and hung on wooden racks to dry in natural fresh cold air (January – April). The drying process takes approximately three to four months, during which 70% of the water is removed and the essential vitamins and nutrients are retained. The de-hydrated fish (STOCKFISH) acquires a peculiar flavor/taste that is totally different from the fresh fish flavor. The nutritional value of 1-Kg of stockfish is the same as approx. 5-Kg of fresh fish. Stockfish is one of the richest known sources of protein, Calcium, Iron and B-Vitamins. Stockfish can be adapted to suite most tastes and palates. When adequately soaked, the fish regains its original weight, and the flesh becomes milky. The fish can be cooked in the same way as fresh cod-fish – poached, fried, creamed or grilled – and can be used in a wide variety of nutritional and tasty dishes.

description:
The London Cure smoked Scottish salmon is what H. Forman & Son is known for. Formans hand prepares every side of salmon, from the filleting to the rope hanging to the pin-bone removal to the hand carving. There's no sugar, no nitrites, no added coloring and no wet brine. You will receive the finest smoked Scottish salmon direct to your door.

Our Story

When Harry (Aaron) Forman arrived in London’s East End from Russia at the beginning of the last century he pursued the trade he knew best – curing fish; in particular, the salmon he imported in barrels of brine from the Baltic. It wasn’t long, however, before he discovered a rich source of fresh wild salmon much closer to home: Scotland.

Inspired by the exceptional quality of fresh Scottish salmon, Harry developed a cure that complemented its unrivalled flavour. The deliciously mild London Cure was born and soon it was the talk of reputable establishments around the capital such as Wilton's restaurant which we have supplied for over 90 years with our genuine wild smoked Scottish salmon.

A century later H. Forman & Son remains a family concern, the last of the original London smokeries, with Lance Forman, Harry’s great grandson, flying the flag for the famous London Cure. Remaining faithful to principles established in 1905 – the freshest salmon, a little salt, just the right amount of oak smoke – he is upholding traditional values and skills that would otherwise have died out long ago, along with one of gastronomy’s finest foods: H. Forman & Son’s Genuine Wild Smoked Scottish Salmon.

The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

title: Fresh, Wild Atlantic True Cod Fillet, 8 oz
bullet_point: [Monterey Bay Aquarium Seafood Watch: Best Choice Rating, Product of United States]
description: In Alaska the fishery is typically January through March with a secondary fishery September through October. Coastal fisheries have a more consistent supply year round, but produce much less tonnage than Alaska. Cod has a mild delicate flavor and firm texture. It is lean with a low fat content, and a good flake. Meat is white to pinkish-white in the fresh state, and pure white when cooked. Cod is one of the most universally used and versatile fish species, as it is caught in so many parts of the world's oceans and used by so many world markets in a variety of product forms. While atlantic and pacific cod are two distinct species, there is very little, if any, difference between the two as product forms. Atlantic cod occupies some eastern United States and European market niches as it has been fished commercially for much longer. As atlantic cod stocks dwindle, however, pacific cod products have made their way into these niches. Pacific cod is also known as true cod, Alaskan cod and "P"-cod. Black cod, ling cod and rock cod are not related to "true" cods.

description:
The History of Angelo Parodi

Angelo Parodi dates to 1888 when the legendary Parodi created  the brand that for over 100 years, has brought to tables all over the world the Italian excellence in tuna and other fish specialties. A long history that has come down to us thanks to the ability of respecting the secrets of tradition combined with the constant search for progress in processing techniques. Angelo Parodi is the precursor of the modern method of conservation and canning of fish. The perfection of the flavor of the products is guaranteed by a strict quality control, the selection of the finest fish, a wise cutting and cleaning technique and finally by giving the seasoning just the right amount of time. Today Angelo Parodi extends his offering by proposing sardines and mackerel from the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts: products that with their characteristics of excellence make Angelo Parodi a legend among lovers of fish preserves.

 

Fishing Areas, Methods and Protection of Marine Resources and Endangered Species

Angelo Parodi does NOT procure fish sourced from the marine reserves of the Pacific or from other reserves and protected areas identified by coastal states. In the procurement processes we consider the use of selective and safe fishing methods and equipment as fundamental to minimizing the incidental catches of immature fish and other species. We consider the protection of the marine environment a priority, so that the natural heritage and biodiversity of the natural waters are preserved.  We encourage the presence of independent international observers on board our suppliers' ships and we do not purchase species deemed at risk of extinction.

description: Spain is fanatical about quality tuna, and Bonito del Norte is the prince of Spanish tuna. Flaked onto a salad or served on toasted baguettes, Bonito del Norte is the most tender, delicate jarred tuna in the world. And the small family company Nardin is among the very finest in Spain. The secret is in the way it is prepared. Fresh Bonito del Norte is poached in sea water, then the tuna loins are hand cut and placed in glass jars. They are then topped off with olive oil, which preserves the tender flaky texture of the tuna. During the fishing season the Nardin family selects the best Bonito del Norte tuna from each morning's catch and prepares it that day fresh at their small facility in the Basque country. They never use frozen fish, another reason why their's is the finest tuna in Spain. Bonito del Norte is a small tuna that migrates from the Atlantic to the rich, cool seas north of Spain every year. There they linger and fatten up on the plentiful smaller fish. This is the moment when the tuna is ripe for harvest. The Spanish fishing boats catch the tuna by hand with fishing poles - never with nets or long lines. This preserves the quality of the fish, which would otherwise be stressed by other harvesting methods. We invite you to try the very best tuna in the world. One of our favorite ways to serve Bonito del Norte is to toast rounds of french bread, place a sweet piquillo pepper on top of each, then a piece of tuna. Broil them for a minute or two until warm. Que maravilla!

Bumble Bee Chunk White Albacore tuna has the same great quality as all of our Albacore products. The only difference is that this Albacore is flaked for your convenience. Albacore is caught in cooler tropical areas of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans during the spring and fall seasons. Bumble Bee only sources the highest quality Albacore, and that is why we are known for our great appearance and flavor of our Albacore products. Not only do we create a high quality product, but all of our canned Albacore items are packaged (canned), in the USA. Here at Bumble Bee we value healthy living, and we have developed recipes that follow that healthy lifestyle we are all trying to achieve. There are a number of recipes that will leave you satisfied without all of the additional calories. Some of our favorites are: Tuna, Veggie, and Wild Rice Salad, Greek Tuna Salad, and Tuna Avocado Melt Quesadillas. We invite you to try all of our Albacore products and tell us what you think.

Bumble Bee solo fuentes de Albacore de la más alta calidad, y es por eso que somos conocidos por nuestra gran apariencia y sabor de nuestros productos Albacora. No solo creamos un producto de alta calidad, sino que todos nuestros artículos de Albacore enlatados están empaquetados (enlatados) en los Estados Unidos. Aquí en Bumble Bee valoramos la vida saludable, y hemos desarrollado recetas que siguen ese estilo de vida saludable que todos estamos tratando de lograr. Hay una serie de recetas que te dejarán satisfecho sin todas las calorías adicionales. Bumble Bee bezieht nur die hochwertigsten Albacore-Produkte. Wir schaffen nicht nur ein hochwertiges Produkt, sondern alle unsere Albacore-Artikel werden in den USA verpackt (konserviert). Bumble Bee Chunk White Albacore tuna יש את אותה איכות מעולה כמו כל מוצרי Albacore שלנו. ההבדל היחיד הוא כי Albacore זה מתפורר לנוחיותך. Albacore נתפס באזורים טרופיים קרירים יותר של האוקיינוסים האטלנטיים, האוקיינוסים ההודיים בעונות האביב והסתיו. Bumble Bee מקורות רק את Albacore באיכות הגבוהה ביותר, ולכן אנחנו ידועים במראה והטעם הנהדרים שלנו של מוצרי Albacore שלנו. לא רק שאנו יוצרים מוצר באיכות גבוהה, אלא גם כל הפריטים המשומרים שלנו של Albacore ארוזים (משומר), בארה"ב. כאן ב-Bumble Bee אנו מעריכים חיים בריאים, ופיתחנו מתכונים שעוקבים אחר אורח חיים בריא שכולנו מנסים להשיג. ישנם מספר מתכונים שישאירו אתכם מרוצים ללא כל הקלוריות הנוספות. חלק מהאהובים עלינו הם: טונה, ירקות וסלט אורז פראי, סלט טונה יווני ואבוקדו טונה נמס Quesadillas. אנו מזמינים אתכם לנסות את כל מוצרי Albacore שלנו ולספר לנו מה אתם חושבים.

تتميز التونة البيضاء بامبل بي تشنك بالنفس الجودة العالية التي تتميز بها جميع منتجات ألباكور لدينا. والفرق الوحيد هو أن هذا البكور مقلوب من أجل راحتك. يتم التقاط البكور في المناطق الاستوائية الأكثر برودة في المحيط الأطلسي ومنطقة المحيط الهادئ والهندي خلال مواسم الربيع والخريف. منتجات بامبل بي هي فقط من الألباكور عالي الجودة، وهذا هو السبب في أننا معروفون بمظهرنا الرائع ونكهة منتجات ألاكور لدينا. نحن لا ننتج فقط منتجًا عالي الجودة، ولكن جميع منتجات البكور المعلبة لدينا معبأة (معبة)، في الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية. هنا في بامبل بي نقدر الحياة الصحية، وقد طورنا وصفات تتبع أسلوب الحياة الصحي الذي نحاول تحقيقه جميعًا. هناك عدد من الوصفات التي ستجعلك راضيًا بدون جميع السعرات الحرارية الإضافية. بعض من المفضلات لدينا هي: التونة والخضار وسلطة الأرز البرية وسلطة التونة اليونانية وأفوكادو التونة المذابة. ندعوك إلى تجربة جميع منتجات ألباكور لدينا ونخبرنا بما تعتقد.

description:
Over 90 years ago, the Season Brand® was the inspiration of a Polish immigrant who started as a food merchant selling specialty products to grocery stores in the Northeast Region. By sourcing the highest quality ingredients Season grew as a trusted brand for specialty fish. In the 1950's, as Season’s reputation as a diversified line of high quality, canned seafood, specialty vegetables grew, Season became a household staple in cities throughout the United States. Today, the Season Brand® continues to source only the highest quality ingredients bringing consumers the superior taste they have known to love.

לפני מעל 90 שנה, מותג Season היה ההשראה של מהגר הפולני שהתחיל כסוחר מזון למכור מוצרים מיוחדים לחנויות מכולת באזור צפון מזרח. על ידי מיקור הרכיבים באיכות הגבוהה ביותר העונה גדלה כמותג אמין לדגים מיוחדים. בשנות ה-50, כאשר המוניטין של העונה כקו מגוון של מאכלי ים משומרים, ירקות מיוחדים גדלו, העונה הפכה למרכיב ביתי בערים ברחבי ארצות הברית. היום, מותג Season ממשיך למצוא רק את המרכיבים האיכותיים ביותר ומביאים לצרכנים את הטעם המעולה שהם מכירים לאהוב.

Vor über 90 Jahren war die Season Brand® die Inspiration eines polnischen Einwanderers, der als Lebensmittelhändler begann, Spezialprodukte für Lebensmittelgeschäfte im Nordosten zu verkaufen. Durch die Beschaffung der hochwertigsten Zutaten wuchs Season als vertrauenswürdige Marke für Spezialfische. In den 1950er Jahren wuchs der Ruf der Saison als diversifizierte Linie von hochwertigen, konservierten Meeresfrüchten und Spezialgemüse an, wurde die Städte in den Vereinigten Staaten zu einem Grundnahrungsmittel. Heute bezieht die Season Brand® weiterhin nur die hochwertigsten Zutaten und bringt den Verbrauchern den überlegenen Geschmack, den sie kennen.

description:
Sustainable Seas Albacore Tuna

Sustainable Seas sources tuna caught only by pole and line. There is virtually no by-catch associated with the trolling or pole and line techniques, which are regarded as the best fishing methods for tuna, a fact worth remembering when you buy.

Pole and line fishing has been practiced for centuries in several different parts of the world. The method involves attracting a school of tuna to the side of a baitboat by throwing live sardines and anchovies overboard. This creates a tuna feeding frenzy and fish are hauled out of the water, one-by-one, using pole and line with an artificial lure attached. The size of tuna caught this way is almost exclusively younger migratory tuna that are also lower in mercury than the older tuna caught deeper with long-lines. Rethink your relationship with the seas.BE SUSTAINABLE

This big tin contains 24 to 30 fish (head off) packed in 3 neat layers. Wow are these delicious! The Baltic sprat, Sprattus balticus is a herring-like, marine fish in the family Clupeidae. It is found in northeast Atlantic Ocean and most of the Baltic Sea, excluding the Bothnian Bay and eastern Gulf of Finland. Young sprats are commonly known as brislings. They has silver grey scales and white-grey flesh. The fish is around 12% fat in its flesh and is a source of many vitamins. When used for food it can be canned, salted, fried, grilled, baked, marinated, and so on. Canned sprats (usually smoked) are available in many north European countries, including the Baltic States, Scandinavia, Germany, Poland and Russia. They are an important Latvian export. There is actually no live fish with the name Sardine. Sardines are made from any of 11 different species of fish—including herring, sild, pilchard, and sprats or brislings. description:
Once a frozen fillet is completely thawed, it can be re-frozen though we do not recommend it, as taste and quality may begin to suffer. No fillet should be re-frozen if it has been thawed 2 days or longer.

The best way to thaw your wild salmon dinner fillet is to leave it in the refrigerator overnight (in its pouch), allowing at least 8-10 hours. Trying to rush the process by thawing at room temperature or placing the frozen pouch in warm water is definitely NOT recommended, as it can cause the salmon to lose flavor and texture. If you must thaw your salmon quickly, place the frozen pouch in a bowl of cool water for 30-45 minutes, and then continue thawing in refrigerator.

TO BAKE: Pre-heat oven to 275°F. Place salmon fillet skin side down on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil, and bake for approximately 20 minutes. Do not flip salmon fillet.

TO GRILL: Brush grill with olive oil PRIOR to heating. Once the grill is medium-hot (you should be able to hold your hand 6 inches above the grill for 5 seconds), brush the top of each salmon fillet with olive oil, and place on grill skin side up. Grill fillet until sides begin to turn opaque. Flip once, and continue grilling until fully cooked.

TO BROIL: Place salmon fillet skin side down on a broiler pan brushed with olive oil, and place on oven’s middle rack. Generally broil about 10 minutes or so, though keep watching to avoid overcooking. Do not flip salmon fillet.

description: Tuna in the perfect size for lunch, dinner or a meal. We love the shape of the can for how it feels in the palm of your hand. And opening it reminds us of those romantic (fantasy or real) wicker basket picnics in a green field in the country of your choice! A pantry must! This is the authentic White Tuna, Bonita Del Norte, from the dense tuna banks in the waters off of the coast of the Basque Country. The fishing boats of Ortiz, the premiere name in seafood packing, capture the fish using traditional methods, which respect the environment and avoid hurting dolphins or any other marine species. Bonita Del Norte (Thunnus Alalunga) is the most oceanic species in the tuna family. They are all warm blooded, pelagic and migratory and they form shoals. The Atlantic White Tuna carries out two migrations in its lifetime, which are easily differentiated by its stage of maturity. Then they return towards their places of origin. Bonita Del Norte fishing takes place in the Cantabrian Sea during the summer months when, coming from the Azores Sea, the fish appear annually in the waters of the Bay of Biscay, where they tend to be located on the warm side of the thermal waters, feeding on horse-mackerel and mackerel eggs and larvae. They cook and pack the tuna in olive oil to preserve the tuna's highly prized flavor. These large chunks will make a beautiful, and of course tasty Salade Niçoise, if you can keep from eating them right out of the jar.
